output:
I found four households with wash sales in 2025: HH-0780, HH-0129, HH-9234 and HH-0363. One more, HH-3058, can't be settled from the files.

All four follow the same pattern. A joint taxable account owned by a married couple filing jointly sold a holding at a loss. Within 30 days, one spouse bought the same security in their own IRA. I prorated the disallowed loss by replacement shares over shares sold.

| Household | Loss sale (joint taxable) | Replacement (spouse's IRA) | Days apart | Disallowed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0780 | T-0780-0022: 879 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, 4 Sep 2025, loss $12,860.65 | T-0780-0031: 390 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, 2 Oct, Nadia's traditional IRA | 28 | **$5,706.09** |
| HH-0129 | T-0129-0035: 642 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, 3 Oct, loss $31,896.36 | T-0129-0037: 360 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, 15 Oct, Jun's Roth IRA | 12 | **$17,885.81** |
| HH-9234 | T-9234-0035: 847 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, 3 Nov, loss $53,516.17 | T-9234-0037: 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, 19 Nov, Ingrid's traditional IRA | 16 | **$31,591.60** |
| HH-0363 | T-0363-0035: 3,192 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, 21 Oct, loss $35,820.62 | T-0363-0037: 1,340 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, 3 Nov, Anika's traditional IRA | 13 | **$15,037.48** |

The four disallowed amounts total $70,220.98. Because every replacement was bought inside an IRA, under IRS Revenue Ruling 2008-5 the disallowed loss probably can't be added to the replacement shares' cost basis. It is likely lost for good.

**Unresolved: HH-3058.** On 12 Dec 2025 Priya sold 1,600 Bramwell Devices Group from an individual taxable account (T-3058-0048). Another 800 Bramwell Devices Group vested in the same account 22 days earlier (T-3058-0047). The custodian lists both sold lots with a $0.00 cost basis ("no cost basis"). The value on the vest dates, which would be the real cost basis, isn't recorded anywhere. Quarter-end prices ($221.19 on 31 Mar, $247.77 on 30 Jun) are well below the $273.61 sale price, so it was most likely a gain. The files can't confirm that, though.

**How I checked:**
- I looked at all 2025 sales in every household folder and found 21 at a loss. Five more had a $0.00 cost basis.
- None of the other loss sales had a same-security purchase or RSU vest within 30 days on either side. Six missed narrowly:
  - HH-0221, HH-0679 and HH-9571: 31 days
  - HH-0380: 35 days
  - HH-0981: 37 days
  - HH-0847: 41 days
- The other four $0.00-basis RSU sales (HH-0376, HH-0816, HH-0221, HH-0984) have no acquisition in the window, so the missing basis doesn't matter there.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/) and the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/).

The advisor asks: which households sold a security at a loss in a taxable account during 2025 and acquired the same security within 30 days before or after the sale, in an account of the seller or the seller's spouse, so that some of the loss is a wash sale?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households did, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household that did, each as {"household_id": ..., "sale_transaction_ids": the loss sales affected, "replacement_transaction_ids": the acquisitions that replace them, "disallowed_loss": the loss disallowed, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
